result.title: Branching On-Policy Distillation
result.summary: On-policy distillation (OPD) provides teacher supervision on student-generated trajectories, but a single trajectory realizes only one continuation at each decision, limiting supervision coverage under a finite sampling budget. We propose BranchOPD (Branching On-Policy Distillation), which selects informative decision points using student uncertainty and teacher-student disagreement, resamples student-policy continuations from shared prefixes, and applies token-level teacher supervision to both main trajectories and branches. BranchOPD operates at token-level decisions in mathematics and within-turn decisions in agent tasks. Shared-prefix reuse reduces student-generated token costs by approximately 19% on ALFWorld and 31% on WebShop relative to seven independent trajectories. We also introduce protocol-boundary repair (PBR), which uses targeted supervision under protocol constraints to mitigate repetition and wasted generation. BranchOPD outperforms Vanilla OPD and Multi-Rollout OPD (n=7) across all evaluated benchmarks, with gains over Vanilla OPD of 18.55 percentage points in mean mathematics accuracy over 16 sampled answers (avg@16) and 13.8 points in mean ALFWorld ID/OOD success. Mechanistic analyses and selection ablations show that branching at uncertain decisions expands subsequent behavior coverage and outperforms random selection and turn-initial branching.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 BranchOPD：用学生不确定性与师生分歧挑选决策点，从共享前缀重采样学生策略分支并对主轨迹和分支施加 token 级教师监督，另加协议边界修复，在数学与 ALFWorld/WebShop 上降低生成开销并提升准确率。
AI.relevance_reason: 按不确定性选择分支点、共享前缀复用与教师分歧信号，可能为 LVR 的轨迹训练、监督贡献分配及推理成本核算提供可核查的方法线索，但论文不涉及视觉或多模态推理。
